tasks.title: Guard against tracked coordination state and clean main
tasks.description: Add a doctor check (coordination:tracked-state) that hard-fails when any path under coordination/claims, coordination/queue, or coordination/handoffs is tracked by git on a normal branch (skipped when checked out on the coordination branch), using the existing git() and currentBranch() helpers. In the same change, verify the CLI never reads the repo-root coordination/ directory as a fallback (it operates on .appbuilder/coordination-worktree), then git rm the 13 stale tracked files and add coordination/claims/, coordination/queue/, coordination/handoffs/ to .gitignore alongside the existing coordination/generated/ entry. Combining the guard and the cleanup in one PR keeps main green on merge. Written test-first.
acceptance_criteria: doctor reports problem coordination:tracked-state (and lists it under failures) when a coordination/claims|queue|handoffs file is tracked on a normal branch, and ok otherwise.
A test creates a git fixture with a tracked coordination/claims file, asserts the failure, then untracks it and asserts the check clears.
After the change, on main, git ls-files coordination/claims coordination/queue coordination/handoffs returns nothing and appbuilder doctor passes.

tasks.title: Make node --test the canonical test command on Windows
tasks.description: Document node --test as the canonical, cross-platform way to run the suite and explain that npm test can fail on Windows because PowerShell execution policy blocks npm.ps1. Update the HOWTO.md prerequisites/test guidance and mirror it in AGENTS.md if it references npm test. Optionally add a warn-level win32 hint to doctor. Docs-focused; no behavior change to the test runner.
acceptance_criteria: HOWTO.md documents node --test as the canonical command and notes the PowerShell npm.ps1 execution-policy caveat.
Any npm test reference in AGENTS.md is reconciled with the node --test guidance.

tasks.title: Add a human-friendly status table view
tasks.description: Add a --human flag to appbuilder status that prints a concise table (claim, branch, expiry, next action) derived from the data deriveStatus() already computes, with next action chosen per bucket (active -> work/handoff, expired -> release --expired, merged_unreleased -> release, orphaned -> prune). Keep JSON as the default output so agents that parse status are unaffected. Written test-first.
acceptance_criteria: appbuilder status with no flag still emits valid JSON (unchanged contract).
appbuilder status --human renders a table with claim, branch, expiry, and next-action columns for an active claim.
A test asserts both behaviors against a fixture with a claim.

tasks.title: Modularize cli/appbuilder.js into cli/lib modules
tasks.description: Behavior-preserving refactor: extract cohesive modules under cli/lib (e.g. git.js, coordination.js, plan.js, validate.js) and reduce cli/appbuilder.js to a command router that wires them together. Isolate the schema validator as its own module so a future validation upgrade has a clean seam (no dependency added now). The existing test suite must pass unchanged as the proof that behavior is preserved.
acceptance_criteria: cli/appbuilder.js is reduced to a router that delegates to cli/lib modules.
The schema validator lives in its own module (cli/lib/validate.js).
The full existing test suite passes with no changes to the tests.
appbuilder doctor and status behave identically to before the refactor.

tasks.title: Add concrete token/session budget guidance
tasks.description: Extend .agent/rules/token-use.md with concrete budgeting guidance only: task-size estimation reusing files_touched_estimate, per-session and weekly budget heuristics, and handoff-compression rules. No new engine, artifact subsystem, or RAG. Optionally add a HOWTO.md pointer. Lowest priority; do last.
acceptance_criteria: .agent/rules/token-use.md contains concrete task-size, session, and weekly budget guidance plus handoff-compression rules, reusing files_touched_estimate.
No new runtime code, dependency, or artifact subsystem is introduced.
